name: HP Latex 330
guidance: HP notes that cross-color ink migration may occur within the same shared printhead after approximately 5–7 days without printing. This is a printhead effect, not a published tube dry-out interval. TAD uses a weekly all-color test print to detect migration and verify that the ink-delivery system remains properly primed; 5-day due-soon and 7-day overdue markers are TAD operational thresholds, not an HP-prescribed print schedule.
storageGuidance: The non-printhead components that can require service are the Ink Delivery System's ink-supply tubes. If the tubes lose prime or contain air, HP service procedures call for Purge Tubes or Refill Ink Tubes; HP does not specify a number of idle days after which this occurs. For extended inactivity, store and park the printer according to HP procedure: unload substrate, park the carriage in the service station, leave ink cartridges, printheads, and the maintenance cartridge installed, then shut down with the front-panel power button followed by the rear switch.

name: Sawgrass SG1000 Dye Sublimation Printer
guidance: Sawgrass recommends at least 1–2 prints per week when the SG500/SG1000 is not used daily and says to leave the printer plugged in and switched on so its automatic cleaning cycle can run every 10 hours.
storageGuidance: Sawgrass recommends leaving the printer powered on during inactivity. If it must be powered off, Sawgrass says to turn it on for a few minutes every 20–25 days; after extended inactivity, run a nozzle check before printing. A head flush is a recovery step after cleaning attempts, not routine storage.
